integration.ancestryNote: The repository permits squash merges only. The exact-head-reviewed candidate was integrated as the single squash commit above, so historical ancestry is replaced, not preserved: the tested head is not an ancestor of Main. Whether the tested head commit OBJECT is still retrievable on a given host is incidental and MUST NOT be asserted either way - GitHub's pull-request checkout (actions/checkout@v4, fetch-depth: 0) fetches the PR head ref and retains that object, while a clone that never fetched the ref does not have it. A prior correction asserted the tested head must not resolve and therefore failed on CI while passing locally; the corrected gate verifies the recorded identities WHEN the object is present and asserts only the host-independent facts (the integrated squash commit's parent is exactly the recorded tested-head parent, the tested head is not an ancestor of HEAD, and the delivered bytes are content-equivalent to the tested bindings).

equivalenceClaims.baseRelation: The integrated squash commit's parent is exactly the recorded tested-head parent, so the squash was applied onto precisely the base the tested head was built on.
equivalenceClaims.contentRelation: Every byte the real run bound (C1 profile/certificate, metric contract, holdout, oracle, typed plan, committed C2 certificate, retained raw evidence) is byte-identical on Main to the tested-run bindings; the product/config/fixture/contract/certificate/profile/C1 bytes are the same objects and were never changed after the tested head except by the bounded real-evidence registration recorded here.
equivalenceClaims.nonClaim: This is content-level equivalence under the repository's squash-only policy. It does not assert, and no test may assert, that the tested head commit is an ancestor of Main.

testedSourceVersusCandidate.checkedBy: content-equivalence: every path bound by the tested run is byte-identical to its committed bytes on Main; the integrated squash commit's parent is asserted equal to the recorded tested-head parent
testedSourceVersusCandidate.note: Every changed path is within the bounded real-evidence registration correction (newly tracked retained bytes, the provenance/readback records that bind them, the source-map updater and its content-addressed outputs, the legacy-identity inventory re-freeze, and the delivery record). rechecks.policy: Re-run only checks whose relevant inputs changed. No product input changed after the tested head, so no historical evidence was re-minted. The focused source-local suites (C2 safe-aggregate, C1 certification, legacy-technical-identity plan, source map) and the canonical npm suite were re-run at the correction head as this correction gate; the actual outputs are recorded in WORK_RESULT.md.

nonClaims: No general PostgreSQL, production, customer-data, HA, scale, performance, extension, or all-PostgreSQL-versions/auth-modes claim; only this isolated disposable loopback clean room with synthetic non-customer bytes is described.

The clean room is bound only to the disposable loopback-only PG 16 deployment named above; the substrate image/volume/back digests are recorded in the delivery record as sha256 prefixes, which is their actual recorded fidelity.
